title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
prompt: You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, both sorted in ascending order, and an integer `k`. Define a pair `(u, v)` as one element from `nums1` and one from `nums2`. Find the `k` pairs with the smallest sums `u + v`, and return them as a list of `[u, v]` pairs, ordered from smallest sum to largest.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 are sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Generating every possible pair and sorting them is O(n*m log(n*m)), far too slow when nums1 and nums2 are both large.

Because both arrays are sorted, the pair (nums1[0], nums2[0]) is guaranteed to have the smallest sum, and every 'next smallest' candidate pair only ever comes from advancing one index of an already-considered pair.

Use a min-heap seeded with pairs (nums1[i], nums2[0]) for the first min(k, len(nums1)) values of i. Each time you pop the smallest-sum pair (nums1[i], nums2[j]), push (nums1[i], nums2[j+1]) if it exists — this explores sums in increasing order without ever generating all n*m pairs.

solution.approach: Since both arrays are sorted, the globally smallest sum must pair nums1[0] with nums2[0]. More generally, if (nums1[i], nums2[j]) is a candidate, then (nums1[i], nums2[j+1]) is the next candidate that could follow it for that fixed i. Seed a min-heap with pairs (nums1[i], nums2[0]) for the first min(k, len(nums1)) indices i, keyed by sum. Repeatedly pop the smallest-sum pair, add it to the result, and if the popped pair's j index has a next element in nums2, push (nums1[i], nums2[j+1]) as the next candidate for that same i. This produces the k smallest sums in order while only ever holding O(k) candidates in the heap at once, without materializing the full n*m grid.
